author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory page
summary: A read-only page listing every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name, on a single page with no pagination. A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear.
acceptance_criteria: When the specialty directory is opened, every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, and all on a single page with no pagination.
A veterinarian holding a specialty is shown by full name, given name before family name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty does not appear on the page; the page lists specialties, not the full veterinarian roster.
A specialty held by no veterinarian still appears, shown with no veterinarians under it.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
notes: Inverse view of the veterinarian directory (REQ-VET-001). Read-only; NG-2 unchanged. URL/route left to system-design per PRD house style of describing pages behaviorally.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the established server-rendered, feature-package page pattern (system-design.md Overview; Contracts rows for VetController and VetRepository). The specialty directory is a second read-only HTML page in the vet package, served by VetController and rendered by a new Thymeleaf template, mirroring /vets.html. The one real adjustment: Specialty extends NamedEntity and carries no back-reference to Vet, so the specialty->veterinarians grouping is an inversion of the Vet.specialties ManyToMany, built in the controller (presentation grouping, not a domain rule). To honor the orphan-specialty edge case the controller also needs the full specialty set, so VetRepository gains an all-specialties query method -- keeping the vet package's single-repository shape rather than adding a SpecialtyRepository, consistent with the owner package's PetRepository/VisitRepository minimization.
integration_points: New route GET /specialties.html handled by VetController, returning view name vets/specialtyList; no request params, no pagination model.
VetController gains a handler that fetches vets (existing findAll) plus all specialties, inverts into an ordered specialty->veterinarians structure, and adds it as a single model attribute.
VetRepository gains a query method returning every Specialty (e.g. @Query("SELECT s FROM Specialty s")), a Repository<Vet,Integer> returning a non-Vet type -- valid Spring Data usage.
New template src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders the grouping with no pagination block; reuse the fragments/layout page shell as vetList.html does.

patterns.description: existing /vets.html server-rendered handler + view-name-return pattern to mirror for /specialties.html
Vet.getSpecialties() sorts specialties by NamedEntity.getName -- the name-ascending ordering precedent for the specialty axis
full-name rendering ${vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName} to reuse for 'Helen Leary' display

risks.risk: Non-deterministic ordering of specialties or of veterinarians within a specialty would make the page and its MockMvc assertions flaky.
risks.mitigation: Ordering is pinned below; enforce it explicitly via ORDER BY or a Comparator, not by relying on set/insertion order.

risks.risk: The new all-specialties query is not cached while VetRepository.findAll is @Cacheable("vets") with no eviction (Open Question 5).
risks.mitigation: Caching the specialties query is optional and safe (no write path for specialties exists), but not required; leave uncached unless it mirrors the vets cache. Do not add an eviction policy under this slice.

notes: Two decisions the PRD deferred, now pinned. (1) ROUTE: GET /specialties.html, handled by VetController, rendering view vets/specialtyList; read-only, no params, no pagination -- symmetric with GET /vets.html. (2) ORDERING (determinism IS required, for UX and stable tests): specialties ordered by stored name ascending, consistent with Vet.getSpecialties(); veterinarians within each specialty ordered by last name then first name (a fully deterministic tie-break independent of display formatting), while still displayed given-name-before-family-name ('Helen Leary'). The 'given name before family name' clause in the acceptance criteria is a display-format requirement, not a sort key, so the sort key is chosen here. Grouping/inversion lives in the controller (presentation concern), not on the Specialty entity -- do not add a vets back-reference to Specialty. Orphan-specialty edge case (specialty held by no vet still appears) is why the full specialty set is fetched independently of the vet list. Verdict minor: existing pattern + a small repository query and a controller inversion; no ADR (route and ordering are not hard-to-reverse trade-offs), no system-design.md pattern change -- doc-sync will reconcile the VetController/VetRepository contract rows and their Implements column (add REQ-VET-003) once the code lands. Reuse the existing VetControllerTests with MockMvc per the test_names in the prd-entry.

findings.description: All five new test methods are missing the `the` prefix required by the naming school (`the{Subject}Should{Outcome}`). The brief (testing-principles.md § Test Naming) says the school applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward; these tests were written on 2026-08-04. Affected: `specialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians`, `specialtyDirectoryShouldShowVeterinariansByFullName`, `specialtyDirectoryShouldOmitVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty`, `specialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesWithoutPagination`, `specialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian`.
findings.fix: Rename each method with a `the` prefix: `theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithItsVeterinarians`, etc. Note the prd-entry `test_names` field specified the non-compliant names — those should also be corrected in the PRD record to stay consistent with the brief.

findings.description: Three assertion lines use raw `List.get(n)` index-based access (`directory.get(1)`, `directory.get(2)`, `directory(result).get(0)`) rather than AssertJ collection-aware navigation. The agent decision checklist item 7 (testing-principles.md) calls out index-based access as the pattern to replace. A failure on these lines produces a raw IndexOutOfBoundsException or loses AssertJ context rather than a meaningful assertion error naming what was expected.
findings.fix: Replace `list.get(n)` navigation with AssertJ's `element(n)` on the list under `assertThat()`. For example: `assertThat(directory).element(1).extracting(VetController.SpecialtyDirectoryEntry::veterinarians, InstanceOfAssertFactories.LIST).extracting(Vet::getLastName).containsExactly("Douglas", "Leary")`. For `specialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian`, use `assertThat(directory(result)).first()` with `.extracting(...)` chains.

findings.description: findSpecialties() has no @Cacheable annotation. Both findAll() overloads on the same interface are annotated @Cacheable("vets"), making specialties the only uncached read on this repository. Every request to /specialties.html therefore causes an extra database round-trip for data (specialties) that is stable clinic configuration. A dedicated cache name (e.g. "specialties") should be introduced rather than reusing "vets", since the cached types differ.
findings.fix: Add @Cacheable("specialties") to findSpecialties(), declare the cache name in the cache configuration alongside "vets".

findings.description: The table column header uses th:text="#{specialties}" (the plural 'Specialties') for a column whose rows each hold one specialty name. No 'specialty' key exists in messages.properties; one must be added across all locale files.

author: feature-implementer
context: Processing REQ-VET-003 review findings. The code-quality-reviewer tagged an autofix (VetRepository.findSpecialties():65-67, bar_clause consistent-with-codebase) asking that @Cacheable("specialties") be added and a new cache name declared in cache configuration, on the grounds that findSpecialties() is the only uncached read while both findAll() overloads carry @Cacheable("vets").
question: The design-block for this slice explicitly decided to leave findSpecialties() uncached (risk note 2: no specialty write path exists, and adding a cache entangles the slice with the un-evicted "vets" cache / Open Question 5, with an instruction to not add an eviction policy under this slice). Adding a cache therefore reverses a pinned design decision and pulls cache configuration into the slice. Should the reviewer's finding be applied (introduce a "specialties" cache), or does the design-block's uncached decision stand? If it stands, please confirm so the finding can be closed as design-superseded; if you want caching, please supersede the design-block with the cache-name and eviction guidance.
stop_state: Findings 2-4 applied (template header singular key, singular specialty message key across all locales, test method the-prefix renames, AssertJ collection navigation). Finding 1 held pending this ruling; not touching VetRepository.java.

author: system-design-expert
answer: The uncached decision stands. Close the code-quality finding (VetRepository.java:65-67) as design-superseded; do not touch VetRepository.java. Reasoning the reviewer's re-review can act on: (1) No performance problem is being solved. findSpecialties() is a single low-cardinality query for stable clinic configuration, run once per render of /specialties.html, a cold non-hot page. The finding asserts an 'extra database round-trip' but names no measured hotspot; caching here is speculative optimization. (2) The finding's own premise defeats it. 'Consistent-with-codebase' would have us copy @Cacheable("vets"), but that very pattern is flagged in system-design.md Open Question 5 as an unresolved invalidation concern: the vet cache has no eviction and no confirmed answer to whether the data changes out of band. Propagating an un-evicted, unbounded-lifetime cache onto a second entity type replicates that open defect rather than converging on a settled pattern. Consistency with the codebase cannot mean cloning an unconfirmed decision the codebase itself has flagged. (3) Scope. JCache requires the named cache be created explicitly (CacheConfiguration.petclinicCacheConfigurationCustomizer creates only "vets"); adding @Cacheable("specialties") without a matching createCache would fail at runtime, so the finding necessarily pulls a change to CacheConfiguration.java in the system package into a slice whose PRD scope is a single read-only page (non-goals: NG-2, no management). Cache-lifecycle decisions are a cross-cutting infrastructure concern that belongs to a dedicated caching slice which can resolve Open Question 5 (eviction/TTL) for both caches together — not to this read page. The design-block at line 4 is not superseded; it stands as written. If the clinic later wants specialty reads cached, raise it as its own slice that closes Open Question 5 first.
notes: Ruling: design-superseded, finding answered by design. The reviewer's observation (findSpecialties is the only uncached read) is factually correct but the corrective it proposes reverses a pinned decision and inherits an already-documented open defect (system-design.md Open Question 5). No durable-memory write needed: the uncached intent is already pinned in the line-4 design-block risk note 2 and the OQ5 entry covers the invalidation gap for the whole repository. Feature-implementer: resume, leave VetRepository.java untouched, the held finding is closed.
